questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to either Australia or New Zealand, so that was kin of a crucial aspect for me. But also to study in an english speaking country. I felt that that would give me the best opportunities to meet the culture and not just explore it but live in the culture. Another crucial aspect were also that it was possible to undertake more analytical subjects at the university. I wasn't really interested in finance why it was important for me to have the opportunity to undertake other subjects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Melbourne a lot. It's such a nice city with a culture that is very similar to Copenhagen. The nature is amazing and the people are so nice! I would recommend to be a part of different social/sports clubs on the university since the culture at the universities for Australians is a lot of self studying. Therefore the classes isn't the best place to meet new friends. But the clubs connected to the university is a great place to meet people. I was a part of the surf club and the dive club and that was where I met all of the people I spoke with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy but off course you are confused about everything because there are so much new information. University stuff was pretty easy since the university offers a place called stop 1 where you can come and ask all sorts of questions and get help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got some help at Stop 1 with my subjects since it was a bit hectic to figure out. I was on a waiting list for multiple of my subjects but they helped me understand the system and told me that people almost always get the subjects they have chosen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. At the moment there is a shortage of housing in Melbourne so even though you got to see a lot of houses it was very difficult to get one because a lot of people were in the same situation. I would recommend house searching before arriving in Melbourne. And also you should be aware that the pricing is a lot higher than Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You should now that even though the small townhouses looks a bit trashy it is probably where you want to live. I lived in some student accommodation right near University of Melbourne but i would have loved staying in a townhouse. The only thing with the townhouses is that they get very cold in the winter because they are very badly isolated.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to registre but it was more difficult to figure out if you should stay on the waiting list in one subject or try to find another. I wrote to the teachers of the subjects i was on waiting list at and they helped.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it's on a website where you wish for 4 different subjects and was classes of those you want to have. Then you can see your calendar with the classes and if you are early with the registration you'll probably get the classes but otherwise you'll be on a waiting list.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got all the classes i wanted but maybe not the optimal schedule because of my late appliance.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: register a bit early and speak with stop1 if you are in doubt of anything. Also you have a couple of weeks go finalise your subject choice such that you can change a subject ion you really don't like it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programs were challenging but not too challenging which was nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one BA subject which was quit easy, and 3 MA subjects which were more difficult. I had two economics subjects, one econometrics subject and one at management. So the level also differed from course to course and subject to subject.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was more like high school in Denmark. 50% of the final grade was given upon assignments during the semester and some also depending on how active you were in classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sports Economics, Sustainable Business Practices, Economic Analysis and Policy, Computational Economics and Business.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic Analysis and Policy was such a fun/exciting subject for an economics student because it gathers all the theory we've learned and uses it to recommend policies. It was a more practical subject and gave a really good overview on how it is to be a policy analyst.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy stuff (cutlery, pots, pans and so on) for the kitchen etc.,

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was a lot more expensive than I thought. Alcohol was more expensive. Coffee was half price compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can imagine. All sports including surfing, diving and so on. Also there were clubs for new students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the surf club was a lot of fun. Ans also just try everything you can the first weeks. My impression is that a lot of it is free the first 1-2 weeks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Great Ocean Road, Tasmania, Phillip Island, Surf at Tourqay beach, go to port melbourne and play volleyball. Further away I went in a campervan from Sydney to Fraser Island. And from Cairns to Whitsundays and to Uluru in Northern Territory. Would recommend all of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very. The culture is quite similar to the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go the the sports/social clubs or try to live with some locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really cultural differences between the Australians and us. But since australia is very close to asia there were a lot of asians, and there were some cultural differences since there were both a language barrier and also just the culture is very different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the open-mindedness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Be a part of the sports/social clubs, 2. Don't be afraid of saying something stupid in class because no one knows you and also they appreciate more that you say something than nothing. 3. Study at the libraries at school or at the student pavilion - they have very nice facilities for that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: coffee around campus is very cheap. and there is a pharmacy on campus where you get discount because you are a student.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: studying at a university alone and be able to do that and have fun/meet new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Start university without knowing anybody and going to classes alone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just talk to people in classes. If you don't give out the vibe that you want to talk they are probably not going to talk to you.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
